title: Possible {name} in source
description: A {name} sits in a configuration or source file in plain text. Anyone who can read the repository can use it to reach the service it names until the value is rotated. Shape-only: the match cannot prove the value is live or that it is not a variable reference.
remediation: Rotate the credential, review the access logs of the service it names for use of the old value, and load the replacement from a secret manager at run time instead of committing it.
limitation: Shape-only heuristic over assignment syntax. Variable references whose names mix letters and digits can match (false positive), and pure letter values without digits are not matched (documented recall boundary). Quoted values are left to DPK-SEC-007.
fp: Variable references that mix letters and digits, and generated identifiers that look like literal secrets. Placeholder words and call expressions are excluded by guards, and EXAMPLE is vetoed by the runtime denylist.
recordDesc: {name} in source grants the access it names to every reader of the repository until it is rotated.
applicability: Environment files, YAML/INI/TOML configuration, connection strings, and source code that may embed {name}.
risk: Service access with the credential's scopes; HIGH severity.
why: A {name} committed to source works for anyone who can read it, until it is rotated.
fix: Review access logs for use of the old value.
Load the replacement from a secret manager at run time.
verifyT: The old value no longer authenticates, and no matching literal remains committed.
reasoning: Gap evidence: DPK-SEC-007 matches only quoted values ((?:password|passwd|pwd)\s*[:=]\s*["'][^"']{4,}["']), so unquoted env assignments (DB_PASSWORD=...), YAML unquoted values (password: ...), and ADO-style connection-string values (Password=...;) pass it without a finding.

Original rule: key position is case-expanded (env ALL_CAPS, code lowercase, ADO Capitalized) and the value must be an unquoted token of 10+ characters mixing a letter and a digit; call expressions (os.environ.get(...)) and placeholder words (changeme, placeholder) are excluded by negative guards.
Non-overlap: quoted values never match here (the value class rejects quotes), so DPK-SEC-007 keeps its territory; the digit+letter requirement keeps pure identifiers like secret_value out.
Boundary tests pin the 9-vs-10 character edge and the pure-letter limitation; malformed and empty assignments are negative cases.
Provenance: original-authored for this pump (Phase 5, Work A); no external rule or signature text was consulted or copied.

cells.name: password value in an unquoted assignment

title: Possible {name} in source
description: A committed {name} was found in a source or configuration file. Anyone with repository access can use it to authenticate to the service the URL names until the credential is rotated. Shape-only: the match does not prove the value is live.
remediation: Rotate the credential in the service the URL names, review its access logs for use of the old value, and load the replacement from a secret manager at run time.
limitation: Matches URL userinfo passwords of 6 to 64 characters that contain at least one symbol character. Pure alphanumeric userinfo passwords of 12 or more characters belong to DPK-SEC-063 instead; pure alphanumeric passwords shorter than 12 characters are matched by neither rule (documented recall boundary).
scopeT: Single-line URL userinfo shape match for {name}.
fp: Documentation URLs that spell userinfo for illustration, and test fixtures that embed punctuation in userinfo. Query-parameter credentials (password=...) are outside this shape and belong to DPK-SEC-103.
recordDesc: {name} in source grants the access it names to every reader of the repository until it is rotated.
applicability: Source and configuration files that may embed {name}.
risk: Service access with the credential's scopes; HIGH severity.
why: A {name} committed to source works for anyone who can read it, until it is rotated.
fix: Review access logs for use of the old value.
Load the replacement from a secret manager at run time.
verifyT: The old value no longer authenticates, and no matching literal remains committed.
reasoning: Gap evidence: DPK-SEC-063 requires a pure alphanumeric userinfo password of 12+ characters ([A-Za-z0-9]{12,}@), so symbol-bearing passwords (p@ssw0rd-style, percent-encoded forms) pass it without a finding.
Original rule: URL scheme + userinfo + ':', then a password of 6-64 characters from the RFC 3986 sub-delimiter set that must contain at least one symbol character, terminated by '@'.

Non-overlap by construction: a password of 12+ pure alphanumerics cannot contain the required symbol, so DPK-SEC-063 keeps its territory (pinned by negative test); query-parameter credentials remain DPK-SEC-103 territory (pinned by negative test).
Boundary tests pin the 5-vs-6 character password edge, the missing-@ malformed case, and the mailto near-miss.
Provenance: original-authored for this pump (Phase 5, Work A); no external rule or signature text was consulted or copied.

cells.name: password containing symbols in a URL
